messages:
alex: Quick sync 1:00 UTC canary for py/ts SDKs. Using dist-tags: pip canary-0.14.0, npm canary-2.5.0. Shadow 4% traffic. Any objections?

frances: No objections, but we had a signing key rotation last week. Ben, can you confirm artifact signatures?

ben: Verified signatures earlier. CI reported one legacy key id but artifact still valid. I'll watch the publish.

deploy-bot: Canary publish scheduled at 1761112240. Jobs: publish-py, publish-ts, verify-signatures. Link: https://ci.redwood.internal/1761112240

docs-kate: I'll prepare a short deprecation note for the legacy sync client (TS) and add migration steps to the release notes.

ben: Smoke showed a small uptick in latencies on chat.generate (~+40ms) for canary cohort. Noticed Nagle settings changed in client socket code.

frances: Hmm. Latency increase could be a regression for low-latency customers. Suggest we keep artifacts but untag canary from latest (pinback) and re-run after revert or tweak.

alex: Agreed. Don't yank artifacts. @deploy-bot please remove latest tag and set latest -> 2.4.1. Keep canary dist-tags for testing.

deploy-bot: Executing: "npm dist-tag rm @redwood/sdk latest || true; npm dist-tag add @redwood/sdk 2.4.1; python -m pip index remove --no-delete redwood-sdk==0.14.0-canary || true". Done at 1761112265.

ben: Re-run smoke after tag flip shows latencies back to baseline. Error rates unchanged.

alex: Plan: hold GA until we fix socket behavior. Target re-run tomorrow 09:00 UTC. Docs will include a note about pinning versions in package.json/requirements.txt and the deprecation blurb. I'll notify account teams.

docs-kate: Drafted notes and opened PR: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/2100

frances: I'll open a small revert PR for the Nagle change and link CI to canary tests.

alex: Thanks all. Moving thread to #release-war-room if we need a wider call.
